title: Budget LevelUp / Listing Lab — Full AI Security Audit
method: Source-read audit (no live exploitation). Scope: budget-levelup worker + public/*.js and listing-lab worker + public/app.js.

findings.title: Cloud vault brute-forceable — ciphertext fetchable by public handle, protected only by a 6-digit PIN
findings.detail: vaultId = SHA-256("blu-vault:"+handle) is derived from the public handle, and /api/backup GET serves the ciphertext to any unauthenticated caller. The only secret left is a 20-bit PIN, exhaustible offline in ~1 minute.
findings.fix: Vault id is now SHA-256(handle+":"+randomToken); dual-read migrates legacy accounts with zero lockout; optional passphrase raises KDF entropy; 2FA mandatory for new accounts; writes/deletes carry a proof-of-possession token.

findings.title: Anyone can overwrite or delete any user's cloud vault (no proof-of-possession)
findings.detail: /api/backup POST/DELETE validate only the 64-hex id shape. Since the id derives from the public handle, a stranger can DELETE a victim's backup or POST garbage, locking them out with a misleading 'wrong PIN'.
findings.fix: Mutations now require the retrieval-secret / proof-of-possession token introduced in C1.

findings.title: Stored XSS via shared 'study' link — esc() does not escape quotes
findings.detail: esc() escaped only & < > (not " or '), yet was used inside double-quoted src/href attributes fed by a stored ?study= blob. A crafted thumb value closes the attribute and auto-fires onerror, no click needed.
findings.fix: esc() now escapes " and '; image/link sinks go through safeImg()/safeHref() so a shared link cannot inject onerror or a javascript: href.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unthrottled access to billable compute (Browser Rendering + Workers AI + Google Translate)
findings.detail: /api/translate (owner's paid Google key), /api/open (billable browser sessions, 12 URLs/req), /api/analyze (~5+ LLM gens), /api/vision (70B model) had no auth, origin check, Turnstile, or rate limit — a direct financial-DoS / open-proxy surface.
findings.fix: Per-IP rate limits added (open 6/min, analyze 10/min, lookup 20/min, backup 40/5min). Turnstile/auth-gating still recommended for full coverage.

findings.title: SSRF / open proxy in /api/open and /api/fetch (no host allowlist)
findings.detail: /api/open passed user URLs straight into page.goto() and returned text + screenshot; /api/fetch checked https only on the initial URL then followed redirects, so an https→internal 302 slipped past. Full render-and-exfiltrate primitive laundered through the origin.
findings.fix: Both endpoints enforce a marketplace host allowlist; /api/fetch uses redirect:'manual' so a redirect can't smuggle past the scheme check.

findings.title: Fixed global KDF salt (all users share one salt)
findings.detail: salt is a compile-time constant identical for every user, allowing precomputed PIN→key tables for a known handle; violates per-record-salt rule and compounds C1.
findings.fix: Recommended: generate a random 16-byte salt at account creation, store alongside the vault, feed to PBKDF2.

findings.title: PBKDF2 iteration count below 2026 guidance
findings.detail: OWASP 2024+ guidance for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 is ~600k. Auth path uses 250k, sync path 100k. Hardening item; the real fix for the auth path is C1's retrieval-secret, not more rounds.

findings.title: Two apps share one KV namespace
findings.detail: Budget vault backups, revocation list and Stripe session codes share a namespace with Listing Lab studies. Prefixes isolate them today, but a future key-handling bug in either worker puts the other app's data (incl. encrypted vaults) in blast radius.
findings.fix: Recommended: give Listing Lab its own KV namespace.

findings.title: Notes editor is a self-XSS sink (per-user only)
findings.detail: Stores ed.innerHTML and re-injects it raw into a contenteditable; crafted markup executes, but only in the same user's own session (notes live in that user's vault).
findings.fix: Optional: sanitize on save or strip event handlers/<script> on load.

findings.title: TOTP is UI-only, not a cryptographic factor; compare is not constant-time
findings.detail: The vault decrypts from the PIN alone, so an attacker with ciphertext+PIN never invokes the TOTP gate — 2FA adds no cryptographic protection to the data. Compare uses === (not constant-time; not remotely exploitable here).
findings.fix: Recommended: mix the TOTP secret into key derivation, or present 2FA honestly as a UI lock only.

findings.title: Recovery kit writes the PIN to disk in plaintext
findings.detail: Recovery kit download contains handle + PIN in cleartext — a 20-bit secret left in Downloads. Deliberate UX tradeoff (no reset possible).
findings.fix: Recommended: add a one-line in-product warning.

findings.title: Decrypted profile lingers in memory after a profile switch
findings.detail: _pendingProfile holds the full decrypted profile during 2FA and is never cleared; after switching accounts, profile A's plaintext can remain referenced. Not persisted or rendered elsewhere.

findings.title: Guest plaintext store not cleared when creating an account without 'bring my data'
findings.detail: createAccount only removes the guest key when bringGuestData is true; decline it and the guest budget stays in localStorage in cleartext for the next person on a shared device.
findings.fix: Recommended: offer to wipe guest data on first real sign-in.

findings.title: Unlock codes are 64-bit-tag bearer tokens with no expiry
findings.detail: mintCode appends only the first 8 HMAC bytes; verifyCode never checks the embedded issue-day for expiry; /api/redeem has no rate limit. Online forgery infeasible at 2^64 — a licensing weakness (codes share infinitely) rather than a break.
findings.fix: Recommended: bind a code to a device/account on first redeem.

findings.title: Dead code webapp/public/app.js with weaker save()/esc()
findings.detail: Not referenced by index.html; defines a weaker save() that writes state to the plaintext guest key unconditionally and a duplicate esc(). Harmless while unloaded, a footgun if wired up later.
findings.fix: Recommended: delete it or fold it in.

verified_clean: AES-GCM IV uniqueness — fresh 12-byte random IV per encryption in both vault and sync paths; no reuse.
Cross-profile in-memory isolation / wipe-on-switch — every switch reassigns the whole state object; no profile-agnostic key holds signed-in data.
save() routing — signed-in state goes to the encrypted vault; plaintext guest key only written when not signed in; strays like settings.aiKey are stripped.
Budget-app XSS discipline — esc() escapes & < > " and is applied at every render sink checked; no single-quoted attribute interpolating user data.
id validation — ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ enforced on all /api/backup methods; ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ on study GET.
Stripe webhook verification — parses t/v1, rejects >300s (replay), recomputes HMAC over t.body, constant-time compare on raw body.
Admin auth & price integrity — bearer compared constant-time; checkout/webhook take price/product only from server-side CATALOG.
Secrets — no committed keys anywhere in tree or recent git history; all secrets are env.* bindings; no secret logged.
